title: Threads Jobs Watcher
excerpt: A scheduled watcher that monitors Threads for Indonesian IT job postings (frontend / fullstack / AI), filters them through a calibrated scoring model, and delivers a Telegram digest plus a categorized markdown archive — running itself every two hours on launchd.
body:
## Overview

Job postings on Threads move fast and bury fast. Threads Jobs Watcher turns that firehose into a daily digest: every two hours (07:00–22:00 WIB) it searches Threads for Indonesian IT vacancies — frontend, fullstack, AI engineer — filters what it finds through a calibrated scoring model, deduplicates against seen posts, and delivers the survivors two ways: a Telegram digest to a private topic, and a full markdown archive (the entire thread content plus metadata, categorized by role) auto-pushed to a private org repo. Runs unattended on macOS `launchd`; a run with zero findings stays silent on purpose.

*(The repo is private — it contains scraping infrastructure and operational details — so there is no public source link.)*

## Architecture & Flow

```
launchd (macOS) ── every 2h, 07:00–22:00 WIB, random minute offset
   └─ runner.sh ── jitter 0–15 min → scraper.py
        ├─ CloakBrowser (stealth Chromium, headed + humanized input)
        │   └─ persistent burner profile: profiles/threads-burner/ (gitignored)
        ├─ per-query search on threads.com → scroll → extract posts
        ├─ filter: anchor terms (required) + keyword score + location hints
        ├─ dedup vs state.json (local, incremental)
        ├─ reports/YYYY-MM-DD/run-*.json → auto-push (private repo)
        ├─ markdown tree → categorized archive (fullstack | ai | frontend |
        │   backend | data | mobile | devops | qa | other)
        └─ Telegram digest → notify.py via `hermes send` (bot-side tokens —
            zero credentials live in this repo)
```

**Why the timing looks like this.** The two-hour cadence with a random minute offset plus 0–15 min runner jitter is deliberate: fixed-interval, on-the-dot requests are the cheapest bot fingerprint there is. The watcher behaves like an inconsistent human instead.

**Filter calibration as config, not code.** `config.py` carries the whole scoring model — `ANCHORS` (a post must contain hiring language at all), `INCLUDE_KW` (+1), `EXCLUDE_KW` (−2), `LOCATION_HINTS` (+1), and a `MIN_SCORE` threshold. Every knob is testable without touching a browser (`test_filter.py` runs the logic against fixtures), so tuning precision/recall is a config edit, not a re-run of a scrape.

**Dual sinks, different jobs.** The Telegram digest is for acting fast (new postings age out in days); the categorized markdown archive is for looking back — full thread bodies under `5-nov-2026/<kategori>/<username>-N.md`, which makes the archive greppable history of the Indonesian IT job market as a side effect.

## Security & Ops Stance

- **Burner account only** — the Threads session belongs to a disposable account; suspension costs nothing
- **Zero credentials in repo** — Telegram delivery goes through Hermes (`hermes send`), so the bot token never appears in code, logs, or printed output
- **Session/state hygiene** — `profiles/`, `.env`, `logs/`, `state.json` all gitignored; logs prune themselves after 14 days
- **Silent-by-default** — no findings means no message; the digest's signal-to-noise is the feature
architecture:
threads-jobs-watcher/  (private)
├── scraper.py            # CloakBrowser session → search → scroll → extract posts
├── config.py             # queries · ANCHORS · INCLUDE/EXCLUDE_KW · LOCATION_HINTS · MIN_SCORE
├── test_filter.py        # filter logic vs fixtures — calibration without a browser
├── notify.py             # Telegram digest via hermes send (token lives bot-side)
├── login_setup.py        # one-time manual burner login (headed window)
├── runner.sh             # jitter + run + log prune
├── push_reports.sh       # report + archive auto-push
├── reports/YYYY-MM-DD/   # run JSONs (gitignored locally, pushed to private archive)
└── launchd plist         # every 2h 07:00–22:00 WIB, randomized offset
…
